affected_system: cross-agency public-service access, workload, quality, and outcome distribution
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of cross-agency minimum-service capacity
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for cross-agency minimum-service capacity
pair needs-based allocation with explicit equity floors and uncertainty with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Need, eligibility, access, requests, service, quality, and outcomes remain separate measures.
Protected and vulnerable group reporting follows privacy, legal, and small-cell safeguards.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for cross-agency minimum-service capacity.

constraints.description: The distributional public-service equity allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: chief equity officer and city performance director
decision_question: How should staff, funds, appointments, language, and field capacity be distributed across groups and areas?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The distributional public-service equity allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for cross-agency minimum-service capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.intervention_mechanism: needs-based allocation with explicit equity floors and uncertainty
independence_key.primary_outcome: eligible population below minimum service coverage

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting cross-agency minimum-service capacity, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: eligible population below minimum service coverage
distributional gap in eligible population below minimum service coverage
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not call area-balanced request capacity demographic equity, delivered service, or improved outcomes.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.
reference_implementation_note: Tier-D template deep.equity.area-balance.v1 (Area-level request balance) supplies a bounded reference workflow for this design axis. The mapping does not establish complete city-specific inputs, external validity, deployment, adoption, or impact.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for cross-agency minimum-service capacity passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate capacity under minimum equitable service guarantees
transportability_risks: Rights, demographics, service rules, need measurement, geography, and reporting access differ.
Administrative denominators may omit eligible or underserved populations.
